g.text: Fourteen research questions, placed by what they quietly assume
Projects from a week-long retreat of researchers in complexity science and contemplative studies (France, 2026).
Position shows how each project explains things and who it assumes can have a mind - not its discipline. Placements are qualitative readings.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 9.6px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #0b0b0b
font-style: italic; font-size: 9.2px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #0b0b0b

g.text: Solid - built on the same hidden picture:

text.style: font-size: 9.2px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #52514e

g.text: 1 Tension theory, biodiversity measure and GPU solvers all picture the world as flows of energy and resources.

text.style: font-size: 9.2px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #52514e

g.text: 2 The tension theory and the Modern-worldview model both picture a mind as competing sub-agents.

text.style: font-size: 9.2px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #52514e

g.text: 3 The Modern-worldview model and process economies: trade cuts ties, gifts bind them.

text.style: font-style: italic; font-size: 9.2px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #0b0b0b

g.text: Dashed arrow - already holds a piece the other question is missing:

text.style: font-size: 9.2px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #52514e

g.text: 4 Amazonian thought, used in the worldview model: 'human' is a point of view, not a property.

text.style: font-size: 9.2px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #52514e

g.text: 5 Enactive cognition: meaning is made between minds, not carried from one to another.

text.style: font-size: 9.2px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #52514e

g.text: 6 The worldview model already answers it: museums as temples, tourism as pilgrimage.

text.style: font-size: 9.2px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #52514e

g.text: 7 In Amazonian ontologies, predation is a grammar of kinship, not its betrayal.

text.style: font-size: 9.2px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #52514e

g.text: 8 Potawatomi 'grammar of animacy' (Kimmerer): other beings are a who, not an it.

text.style: font-size: 8px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: end; fill: #8a8984

g.text: Axes: Barbier's explanatory archetypes (x) and Descola's ontologies (y). Honest Science retreat, CSCSC, INTP.science.
